functional_semantics.triton: out[r] = (sum_c x[r, c]) / N in float32 for a 2-D row-major x with dim == 1; output (M,) float32 (impl_triton.py 25-30, 58).
functional_semantics.cutile: out[row] = (sum_c x[row, c]) / N in float32; output (M, 1) float32 returned as a squeeze(1) view of shape (M,) (impl_cutile.py 34-40, 60, 86).
functional_semantics.note: Both realise the reference x.mean(dim=1, dtype=torch.float32) (impl_torch.py 5); the generator always passes dim = 1 on a 2-D tensor (tensors.py 451-453).

stages.triton: One kernel; each program owns a small group of rows, strip-mines the columns into a lane-wise float32 accumulator, reduces across lanes, divides by N and stores (impl_triton.py 18-30).
stages.cutile: One kernel; one CTA per row, same strip-mined lane-wise float32 accumulation, cross-lane sum, divide by N, store into an (M, 1) buffer; plus a host-side metadata squeeze (impl_cutile.py 26-40, 86).
stages.note: Identical reduction structure; rows per program and the (M,) versus (M, 1) output buffer shape are layout choices. The squeeze is metadata-only.

dependencies.triton: Rows are independent; the column loop is sequential within a program (impl_triton.py 20-26).
dependencies.cutile: Rows are independent; the column loop is sequential within a CTA (impl_cutile.py 27-34).

reduction_scan_sort.triton: Two-level sum: sequential lane-wise accumulation over column chunks in increasing column order, then one cross-lane tree sum; mean = row_sum / N as float32 true division; masked columns contribute 0.0 (impl_triton.py 25-29).
reduction_scan_sort.cutile: Two-level sum: sequential lane-wise accumulation over column tiles in increasing order, then one cross-lane sum; mean = sum / N as float32 true division; zero-padded columns contribute 0 (impl_cutile.py 28-36).
reduction_scan_sort.note: Same reduction class; the internal order of the cross-lane tree is the DSL's and is not pinned by either source. The reference uses its own float32 summation order, so only tolerance-level agreement is required.

precision.triton: Each loaded chunk is cast to float32 before accumulation; accumulator is float32; divide in float32; output float32 for fp16/bf16/fp32 inputs (impl_triton.py 18, 25, 29).
precision.cutile: Each loaded tile is cast to float32 before accumulation; accumulator is float32; divide in float32; output float32 (impl_cutile.py 26, 28-33, 36).

preprocessing.triton: x2d = x.contiguous() for the 2-D/dim == 1 case (no-op); the generic path permutes the reduced dim last and copies, never taken by the benchmark; allocate out (M,) float32 (impl_triton.py 49-58).
preprocessing.cutile: Same contiguous()/generic-permute code; allocate out (M, 1) float32 (impl_cutile.py 49-60).
preprocessing.note: Both carry the same untested generic-dim path; for benchmark inputs there is no data movement before the kernel.

intermediate_storage.triton: None in global memory; accumulator is a register tile (impl_triton.py 18).
intermediate_storage.cutile: None in global memory; accumulator is a register tile (impl_cutile.py 26).

mutation.triton: x is read-only; fresh output per call (impl_triton.py 25, 58).
mutation.cutile: x is read-only; fresh output per call (impl_cutile.py 29, 60).
mutation.note: Neither side mutates the input; the contract forbids mutation.

hardware_dispatch.cutile: No hardware branches; allow_tma=False and latency hints on loads/stores are lowering hints, not branches (impl_cutile.py 30-31, 40).
hardware_dispatch.note: Single code path on both sides.

fq_boundary.note: bytes_expr counts the single read of x, which both timed run() bodies perform with no preprocessing traffic and nothing prepacked. It omits the M float32 output writes (M * 4 bytes), which every implementation must perform and which are at most about 0.4 percent of the counted traffic over the sweep (M fixed, N >= 1024, config.yaml 8-13). The omission is inherent to the operator, not an implementation-specific boundary difference, so the boundary is treated as consistent; the metric gap is listed as a non-blocking review item. flops_expr counts one add per element and ignores the M divides.

review_items: Non-blocking metric accuracy: bytes_expr 'M * N * dtype_size' omits the M * 4-byte float32 output write that every implementation performs; decide whether to change it to 'M * N * dtype_size + M * 4' (at most about 0.4 percent over the sweep; does not affect the contract text).
